title: Port command deadline races, abort reasons and late-result handling
scope: Complete limited() race over an owned timer/body event boundary, preserving registration/reaction order, shared timeout reason, timer cleanup and late body handling. Clock backend scheduling and retaining/driving body tasks remain required integration. Reuse one shared owned JS numeric formatter.
acceptance: Full original limited body runs deterministic injected-clock schedules before Rust; compare successful/error values, abort identity, clock requests/cleanup, late state and event order, including simultaneous outcomes.
Native ownership/capability bounds, shared formatter callers, Wasm and full source gates pass without dropping inputs or tolerances.
open_items: Actual native/browser timer backend policy, executor and command integration remain required.
The owner must retain body work after a caller timeout; timeout does not authorize dropping partial effects or adding a new session-epoch policy.
Typed clock registration/clear are trusted and serial; host timer resource failures and arbitrary Promise subclasses remain outside this admitted boundary.
